newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas prices mixed, driven by weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas prices mixed, driven by weather.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices were mixed Thursday, with Gulf prices rising in anticipation of colder temperatures in the Northeast and Texas on Friday, market sources said.
Gulf Coast prices gained about 40 cents to the high-$4.60s, with deals reported done in the $4.60-$4.80 range.
South Texas prices jumped about 10 cents to the mid-$4.60s as well-below-normal temperatures were forecast for the state Friday. However, milder air is expected to return by Sunday.
Further east, where storage levels are more than 20 percent ahead of year-ago, New York city-gate prices rose by more than a $1 to the $6.00-6.70 range.

Temperature lows in the teens are forecast for the Mid-Atlantic states Friday and into the weekend. A warming trend is expected to bring temperatures back to near-normal by Wednesday, Weather Services Corp said.
In the Midcontinent, where relief from the frigid weather is expected to arrive this weekend, prices lost about 25 cents to the $4.80-4.85 range, still about 60 cents over January indices.
Because of the critical days declared by Midwest utilities for Friday deliveries, Chicago city-gate prices remained strong in the $5.50-6.25 range. Most traders anticipated a drop in prices Friday.
"People are going to try to take advantage of the warmer weather and put some gas back into storage, but spot purchases should drop off quite a bit," one Midwest trader said.
AGA said stocks in the Producing Region as of Jan 10 were down an additional 35 bcf to 440 bcf, or 49 percent of capacity. These data are compared with 484 bcf a year ago.
In west Texas, Permian gas prices fell by 35 cents to the $4.60-4.65 area, with deals reported done in the $4.10-4.85 range.
Similarly at Waha, prices tumbled more than 30 cents to about $4.70, pressured by milder temperatures in the Southwest.
AGA said Wednesday that gas stocks as of Jan 10 in the Consuming Region West were down 17 bcf to 265 bcf, or 80 bcf behind year-ago levels.
